candidates.exact_span: EPA proposes a revision to the facility temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L to 449 mg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the operative enforceable TDS limit is the proposed 449 mg/L, the prior 497 mg/L, or a temporary limit not yet in effect changes which numeric standard is used for TDS compliance comparisons in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The proposed TDS permit limit, in accordance with 40 CFR §133.101(f), was based 95th percentile of the most recent three years (i.e., 2018-2020) of City's wastewater treatment plant effluent net TDS data.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether this limit is proposed versus final, how §133.101(f) governs applicability, and whether the 2018–2020 basis period defines the enforceable limit could change which TDS numeric limit is deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span: The 30-day average mass loading limit is, also, revised to 24,992lbs/day from 27,664 lbs/day based on the proposed 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 449 mg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of whether the revised 24,992 lbs/day or prior 27,664 lbs/day mass loading limit applies directly changes TDS mass-loading compliance evaluation against reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: The facility is required to continue maintaining the formulated BMP activities and monitoring its effluent quality and quantity on a regular basis with reporting results monthly.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the continuing BMP and effluent monitoring obligations, the meaning of 'on a regular basis' versus monthly reporting, and whether these requirements were applicable in FY2025 affects which monitoring was required (B) and how missing or non-numeric results should be classified when expected monthly reports are absent (C).

candidates.exact_span: The facility is designated a major POTW for permitting purposes and must supply the expanded pollutant testing list described in the EPA Application Form 2A.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Major POTW designation and the scope of the Form 2A expanded pollutant testing list determine which pollutant-specific monitoring requirements are treated as applicable for the facility in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The EPA conducted a water quality screen which is based on the March 15, 2012 NMIP to determine if discharged pollutant concentrations demonstrate RP to exceed WQS for the various designated uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which NMIP version, designated uses, and reasonable-potential screen outcomes are treated as governing affects whether effluent limits are derived and imposed for pollutants evaluated under the screen, changing applicable numeric limits.

candidates.exact_span: If RP exists, the screen model will calculate the appropriate permit limit needed to be protective of such designated uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and how reasonable potential triggers calculation of permit limits, and what limit values the screen model produces, determines which enforceable numeric limits apply to screened pollutants.

candidates.exact_span: The result of the preliminary RP analysis (see Appendix 2) indicates that Cyanide has RP to violate WQS consistent with the designated uses for the receiving waterbody. The draft permit will propose a daily maximum and monthly average limits of 22 ug/L and 14.67 ug/L,
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether cyanide reasonable potential is established, whether limits are only draft/proposed versus enforceable, and which of the stated daily maximum (22 ug/L) and monthly average (14.67 ug/L) limits apply—and for which averaging period—changes cyanide limit applicability and exceedance determinations; the segment also ends mid-sentence, leaving uncertainty about additional limit terms.
